Friday I was talking to my girls about their old school in England, and mentioned how sad I was that #2 never got to have a particular teacher that #1 had, because he left the school the year before she got there. This teacher, Mr. M., was a total champion for #1 when she was dealing with some vicious bullies at that school; he was extremely supportive, he was angry on our behalf, he took #1 under his wing (so to speak) and went out of his way to include her (especially in drama stuff, as he taught drama and English) and support her. He was always very much in contact with us--I have dozens of emails we exchanged--about what was going on and always telling us what a delightful, special, smart girl she was, how she had such a great sense of humor, how much he liked her, and always telling her that she was worth ten of the bullies and what a bright future he thought she had. He left the school unexpectedly about a year and a half before we moved away; we asked and were told that he'd had a family emergency back in Ireland and had needed to move right away.

So as I'm telling #2 how great he was, #1 says, "You know he got in trouble for, like, touching some kids or something, right?"

Well, no. Obviously I did not.

Turns out Mr. M., the man Husband and I liked so much we discussed inviting him over for dinner (and didn't only because we didn't know if it would be appropriate), is currently in prison because he had been using an app on his phone to secretly film girls--female students at the school--changing clothes in the drama room. (Get THIS: One girl wrote on the school's unofficial FB page that he was "a paedo," and the school punished her for it and took it down, but didn't bother to ask her why she'd written that!!!) Turns out, he'd taken an upskirt photo of a female student and kept it on his phone.

Worst of all, turns out he'd gone online and downloaded a file containing images of girls ages 8-14, fully naked, in provocative, fully-exposed poses.

Husband and I are both absolutely stunned by this. We both had actually thought something seemed a little "off" with him--we'd discussed it after first meeting him--but honestly, we suspected he was gay and thought perhaps the "oddness" came from being in the closet. But we genuinely thought he was a wonderful man and teacher, and in fairness (to us, not him) he truly was wonderful when it came to helping #1 and seeing that her bullies were actually punished finally (as opposed to what happened the year before he became her advisor, when they'd basically be pulled out of class in a group and told, "That's not very nice, okay?" We all know how intimidating it is when you're twelve to get out of class with all your friends to be lectured by a wimp and asked to please be nicer, right, because you might get punished for it at some point, maybe, if you don't stop--especially when this happens numerous times with no punishment ever given? :rolleyes. Aaaanyway.)

1 assures us that he never made any off-color or sexual comments to her, not once; that he never touched her in any way that even came close to being inappropriate, that he never said or did anything that made her the least bit uncomfortable. And we believe her; she genuinely wouldn't lie about that--she's a very truthful child by nature, and she knows how important the truth is in this instance.

But we know she changed in that props room. We have photos of her in her costume changes.

I've emailed the prosecutor to explain the situation and ask if it's possible for us to send her some photos of #1 to check against the girls whose pictures etc, he took--the news story said there are a few girls they were unable to identify. Hopefully I'll hear something back from her soon.

But we are, like I said, just stunned by this. And furious, because the school knew about this before we left and never bothered to get in touch with us and tell us about it, ask if #1 had ever said anything about him making comments etc. or if he'd ever been inappropriate with her--and they knew she was one of his "pets," they knew he spent a lot of time with her, they knew that he was our main point of contact at the school and that we had a close relationship with him (close as parent-teacher relationships go, I mean), they knew that she was very involved in his drama stuff. They knew all of that but never said a word, and they knew what he'd been doing at least three or four months before we left.

So...yeah. That was not a fun thing to find out. Apparently his excuse was that after the break-up of his long-term relationship he was very lonely and lost; he claimed (truthfully, it seems) that he'd stopped with the pictures etc. on his own because he couldn't stomach how wrong it was anymore, and he started going to counseling. I guess it makes some sense, though it doesn't excuse it and the downloaded file makes it really hard to believe it was just that he was weak and they were almost-legal or actually-legal and he slipped out of loneliness and misery. Are you sure you're not extremely active, hon? Because I often see you talking about doing an hour + on the Airdyne and then more exercise after that. I'm not saying you're wrong (or that the amount of exercise you do is wrong!), just that biking twenty/thirty miles a day five days a week seems "extremely active" to me. Please forgive me--I don't mean to hurt or upset you, I'm saying this because I genuinely care about you; and I'm also very aware that I don't know how much exercise you're doing/what your typical day is like, this is purely conjecture/guessing in an attempt to help--but I know you've had ED issues, so I wonder if you're not "not seeing" how much exercise you genuinely do. I also wonder if the exercise plus weights/strength training is putting you at a bit of an iron deficiency or other nutrient deficiency, so that's what's going on?

I know when I was on 1200 calories/day, I didn't have periods, and I still go through spells where I skip them for months at a time due to low calories or extra exercise. (I am also generally only having them intermittently in the last couple of years, but whether that's due to weight/calories/exercise or to pre- or peri-menopause I'm not sure; I am almost 46, so it's about time for the baby factory to shut down completely. :-( Husband and I haven't been using any kind of birth control for a couple of years now without a pregnancy, so we're pretty sure it's not a possibility anymore and the semi-rare periods I do get are just hormonal [i.e. no egg, just lining].)

You are also young, though; were your cycles regular before? How long ago did you start or get out of treatment--maybe gaining weight after so long has thrown your cycle out of whack?

Is your mother nearing or in menopause, and how much time do you spend with her? We think the periods I've been getting have a lot to do with our daughters's cycles, since they generally start within a couple of days of each other, and then if I'm going to get one it starts within the next week. Women do synch up if we spend a lot of time together, so I wonder if that could have something to do with it? (I'm not a doctor, of course, so this is, again, just conjecture.)

And of course, are you sure you're not pregnant? (Somebody has to ask, right? :-))

No matter what it is, if your doctor isn't worried then you don't need to be. It's not entirely unusual for women to skip periods, even several months in a row. Some women even do it deliberately, by not taking a break from birth control pills, and there are to my knowledge no real health problems with this. After our second was born I had a Mirena coil and, after bleeding solidly for a month or so immediately following implantation (installation?) I didn't have a period for five years. So there generally aren't any real problems with skipping.

I do suggest, though, that you visit a gynecologist for a pelvic exam, if you haven't already. I've heard stories about women missing periods due to minor blockages or whatever--I am pretty certain that's not the case here (like, I'm 99% sure it's not), and I definitely don't mean to scare you, but I think it would probably be reassuring for you to just go get an exam and see what the gyn says. If you've never had a pelvic exam, I promise you they're not that bad, and I'm sure your mom or another woman you trust would be happy to go with you if you want. They are a necessary part of being a woman, or they will be when you're a little older, so you might as well get that first time over with now.

(I'm pretty vocal about the need for pelvic exams and pap smears; when I was 22/23 I had cervical dysplasia, which is pre-cancerous cells on my cervix. It was caught during a routine pap smear and I was given a LEEP biopsy, which removed all the cells and I haven't had an abnormal pap since. The big thing, though, is that although I had dysplasia I did NOT have HPV, which is a virus that causes many cervical cancers/dysplasias. Now that there's an HPV vaccine I think people assume you can't get cervical cancer if you've been vaccinated/that all cervical cancers come from HPV, and that is NOT the case. So I can be pretty pushy about reminding women to get those smears! Most women your age don't need them if they're not sexually active, but again, I think having an exam would be a good idea for you just to make sure everything is okay and put your mind at ease.)

Again, I hope I haven't upset you, and it's not at all my intention to hurt your feelings or patronize you. I assure you, I in no way think of you as "just a kid" who can't figure things out on her own or whatever. You're just the same age as my daughters--you're right in between them, actually--and you remind me of them quite a bit, so... I genuinely apologize if you feel I'm overstepping or talking down to you. I hope you don't feel that way. {{hug}}
